text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. Most APIs work over HTTP requests, where your application sends a request to a server and receives a response. The data usually comes back in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or a token, to prove who you are. You should also respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, good error handling is essential, because things can go wrong, and your code should respond gracefully instead of crashing.
